options.content:
The JVM, HTTP and trace views for this service live in **Technical → Service Deep Dive** (pick `abofonsa-preview`) and **Apps RED Overview**; it appears there automatically because the agent emits `jvm_*`. This dashboard covers the one thing those cannot show: whether the **signup funnel** is working.

A launch page whose signups have quietly stopped — an over-eager honeypot, an SMTP failure, a rate limit set too low — returns HTTP 200 to everything and looks perfectly healthy on request rate and error rate. `rejected` or `throttled` climbing while `accepted` falls is what makes that visible.

Counts here are **not** the source of truth. `capture_event` and `waitlist_signup` are, and everything is recomputable from them; these are a live view, and a restart resets them.

panels.title: Waitlist submissions by outcome
panels.description: accepted = a new row. duplicate = an address already on the list. rejected = failed the honeypot or dwell-time check. throttled = over the hourly cap for that client.

panels.title: Opt-in outcomes
panels.description: confirmed = double opt-in completed. invalid = a token that was already used, expired, or never existed. unsubscribed = an opt-out honoured.

panels.title: Confirmation emails that failed to send
panels.description: The signup is still captured when this fires — but the person can never complete an opt-in they never received, so they are stranded mid-funnel. Any sustained non-zero value here is a broken SMTP configuration.

panels.title: Failed sign-in attempts
panels.description: bad-credentials = a wrong password. throttled = a client refused before its password was checked, having failed ten times in fifteen minutes. There is one account, so a sustained rate here is somebody guessing at it.
